headline_marked: 25 injured as [[clashes over bus stand control halt traffic]] on Dhaka-Barishal highway
headline: 25 injured as clashes over bus stand control halt traffic on Dhaka-Barishal highway
summary: Rival groups fought for dominance of the Pukuria Bus Stand in Faridpur, blocking the highway for three hours and leaving hundreds of vehicles stranded.
details: Clashes between two rival groups over control of the Pukuria Bus Stand in Bhanga upazila of Faridpur left at least 25 people injured and halted traffic on the Dhaka-Barishal highway for three hours.
The highway was blocked around 9:45 am, leaving hundreds of long-distance buses and other vehicles stranded on both sides, causing immense suffering to commuters.
Police fired several rounds of tear gas to disperse the crowd, but the situation only returned to normal around 12:50 pm after police managed to bring the situation under control.

The conflict involved supporters of Sultan Matubbar of Manikdah union and Siru Molla of Hamirdi union, stemming from a long-standing dispute between residents of 10 villages in Hamirdi and five villages in Manikdah.
The latest violence was triggered after Abdul Kalam, a resident of Maheshwardi village, was allegedly assaulted at the bus stand the previous evening.
In retaliation, residents of Maheshwardi village marched to the bus stand around 7:00 am, sparking the first round of violence that disrupted traffic for nearly half an hour.
The rival groups later regrouped and resumed fighting at 9:30 am, using bricks and locally made weapons to attack one another.
A physician at Bhanga upazila health complex reported that 12 people were brought in, with five admitted and two seriously injured patients referred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital.

headline_marked: Hundreds stranded as [[locals block Dhaka-Tangail highway]] over power outages
headline: Hundreds stranded as locals block Dhaka-Tangail highway over power outages
summary: Protesters in Mirzapur, Tangail, blocked the road for nearly two hours, citing unbearable daily life due to prolonged load shedding.
details: Hundreds of vehicles were stranded on the Dhaka-Tangail highway today after locals in Tangail's Mirzapur upazila blocked the road in protest against prolonged power outages.
The blockade began around 11:30am near the REB power substation in the Jamurki area, causing severe traffic congestion in the sweltering heat.
Protesters claimed that frequent load shedding has made daily life unbearable, with many areas remaining without electricity for four to five hours a day.
Demonstrators highlighted that businesses have been disrupted and students preparing for HSC examinations are struggling due to the outages.
Tangail Palli Bidyut Samity General Manager Chhanowar Hossain stated that the outages were caused by a supply shortfall, with demand being 191MW but receiving only 101MW.
Obaidur Rahman, superintendent engineer of the BPDB in Tangail, added that the district requires 140MW of electricity but is receiving a maximum of 110MW.
The highway was eventually reopened around 1:15pm following police intervention.
